# Ordinary Add retains the recipe lock after Running

Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b

## TLDR

One ordinary Tensorlake host whose sandbox is Running but whose SSH gateway is unavailable delays other launches and completion of builds/preparations using its recipe. Billed builders may remain alive while publication waits. This is extra serialization across transport readiness, not a demonstrated permanent deadlock.

## Details

The caller acquires lock_snapshot_use at tensorlake_add.rs:1352, retains source_guard at 1360, awaits create_host_sandbox at 1378-1380 and drops the guard only at 1385. The helper passes None as create_recorded's guard and Some(self.backend) (1599-1616). tensorlake/hosts.rs:471-484 observes Running and drops only that None; :485-497 then awaits wait_tensorlake_ssh while the real caller-owned guard remains held. Previously the explicit readiness wait followed the outer drop. The ordinary production task is independently spawned (tensorlake_add.rs:903-911), so browser request loss does not cancel this wait or release the lock. Its error propagates with ? and drops source_guard on unwind; normal success drops it at 1385. Host removal cannot cancel this active operation: hosts.rs:1385-1393 and :1435-1445 first try its held provisioning lock and return busy. delete_registered_host aborts only once that separate guard permits removal (service.rs:2125-2155); abort_run at 2195-2203 is test-only. Whole task/runtime cancellation drops the async future's owned guard; it is not a leaked mutex guard. No recursive lock acquisition or wait for a peer that itself requires the source lock was found in the gateway wait, so there is no established permanent cycle.

The production wait_sandbox_ssh uses a 60-second retry deadline, 15-second individual run_shell calls and one-second retry pacing (provisioning/tensorlake_backend.rs:58-89). run_shell awaits capture_child (backend.rs:911-939); timeout kills/reaps the child group and drains pipes within CAPTURE_PIPE_GRACE (:1979-2019,2251-2278). The 60 seconds is a retry budget, not a strict 60-second wall-clock cap: the last attempt and cleanup can extend it. This synthesis therefore replaces any implication of an exact hard 60/75-second total with nominally about a minute plus bounded command/pipe cleanup and normal OS reap/scheduling assumptions. The source shows no permanent recipe-lock deadlock caused by this change.

Competing session create takes the same source mutex (tensorlake/hosts.rs:227); built/prepared publication also takes it (tensorlake/build.rs:1245,2443-2445). Contract: SPEC_impl.md, Tensorlake prepared snapshots: "One per-recipe async mutex excludes source selection/create through the first observed Running state from snapshot publication and deletion. Installation and supervisor attachment run outside that exclusion." Transfer the real outer guard into create_recorded, or retain ordinary Add's readiness wait after the outer drop. g051/c3's preparation ownership and c6's bounded readiness checks neither release nor refute this outer guard.

Suggested bucket: other (bounded launch/build delay and unnecessary billed-resource lifetime). Could-be-highest: no established security or work-loss route. Confidence: confirmed source/contract analysis, not observed execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Caveats: new ordinary prepared Add only; recovery with no selected source and provider-based session launches lack this outer-guard mismatch. Post-Running store-read failure also exits via ? and drops the guard. No reproduction or runtime tests performed. Only the unrelated sealed-host patch subsequently changes this file in the assigned range.

event.summary: Prepared environments can retain an inherited obsolete bundled tmux
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 500548b9253b07a26fd03119679184b69544e31d. TLDR: a user-supplied Linux base with an old ~/.local/lib/farhelm/tmux and no supervisor database can be prepared and launched successfully while keeping that obsolete copy first on sessions' PATH. Ordinary Linux setup removes it, but environment preparation explicitly skips the removal. The rationale that copied-state and setup-managed checks prove no old installation is too strong: prepare checks ReachOutcome::SetupManaged (snapshot_preparer.rs:75-90) and check_copied_state only tests absence of state/supervisor.db, including a dangling link (provisioning/tensorlake_backend.rs:188-198). Neither checks lib/tmux. A custom image/snapshot can retain the binary after its state and managed unit were removed, or after incomplete installation. The preparer reuses the normal Farhelm lib path, writes the new unit with that directory first on PATH, skips RemoveBundledTmux (109-119), and publishes facts after clearing only state. Fresh environment launch intentionally omits ordinary installation, so no later RemoveBundledTmux action runs on that clone (56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:501-620). Contract: SPEC.md:182-189 says 'Every Linux setup and Update plan therefore removes that file as a step of its own, after the supervisor is started or restarted, and a tmux typed in a session afterwards no longer runs that copy.' (Original uses Markdown backticks around tmux.) plan.rs:244-263 itself names the shadowing consequence and intended no-file assumption. Suggested fix: execute the removal during preparation with appropriate warning/error policy, or establish absence before skipping it. Suggested bucket: other, obsolete executable selection in a custom image rather than a demonstrated security or loss-of-work impact. Could-be-highest: no established vulnerability or data-loss route; do not infer one from the word obsolete. Confidence: likely, with exact input premise that a user-supplied base contains the private binary but no supervisor database or setup-managed unit; source proves behavior for that premise, not that a deployed user's image has it. Checks performed: complete preparer and installation dispatcher, plan removal contract/path, copied-state implementation, and pinned SPEC behavior. No reproduction performed. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Caveats: ordinary hosts do remove the binary; standard clean bases do not contain it; Farhelm itself no longer invokes tmux, so impact is only explicit user/agent tmux commands or startup scripts resolving that inherited executable. The comments intentionally exclude preparation, but the checked predicates do not enforce their stated reason.

Podman likewise calls needed before its build/preparation job (environment/podman.rs:994-1022); its launcher reaches the same poll once 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462 adds the container UI (create_form.rs:6099-6114).
